newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish government makes budget pact with left.
newsitem.headline: Danish government makes budget pact with left.

text.p: Denmark's minority government agreed a pact with the far-left opposition overnight, guaranteeing passage of its 1997 budget and ensuring its survival for the immediate future, state radio said on Thursday.

The government won the agreement of the Socialist Peoples' Party (SPP) to a deal balancing the public sector budget by liquidating a maritime war damage fund and a state property agency and transferring money from a workers' holiday fund.
The SPP agreed to support the budget in parliament, in return for increased funding for education, social projects and improved health and safety at work measures.
As part of the deal, the radical Unity List is expected to abstain, rather than vote against the budget, the Danish news agency Ritzau said.
Doubts about the government's stability arose after it failed to agree with the Conservative or Liberal opposition parties over its plans to raise taxes.
With only 76 seats in the 179-seat parliament, it was forced to seek support from the far left but the Unity List had threatened to vote against the budget and topple the government.
Details of last night's agreement have not yet been made public. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969650.
